name: VerifyID – Age Verification for WooCommerce
author: VerifyID ApS

sections.description:
VerifyID checks the age of customers who buy age-restricted products (alcohol, tobacco, nicotine, knives, games and similar) with the national eIDs MitID and Swedish BankID.

  • One plugin, both methods. Enable MitID, BankID or both. The customer’s location picks the language: Denmark gets Danish, Sweden gets Swedish, Norway gets Norwegian texts, and every other country follows your policy. With both methods enabled, the pop-up shows both buttons (MitID first), so the customer can pick either; a cart that needs 19+ or more shows BankID only, and strict country mode limits the methods per country.
  • Age choice on every product. Each product offers 16+, 18+, a higher BankID age or “No verification”, or follows its categories and shows the age that applies.
  • Setup wizard and admin. A step-by-step setup wizard and a VerifyID admin area (overview, settings, tools) get the shop ready in a few minutes.
  • Language switch. Dansk / Svenska / English / Norsk at the top of the verification box.
  • Checkout box everywhere. The Checkout block, the classic checkout, the cart, the pay-for-order page, an optional age gate for every page, and a page that works without JavaScript.
  • Enforced on the server. Every order path is checked on the server: classic checkout, the Checkout block (Store API), pay-for-order, REST API orders, express payment buttons and the Nordic embedded checkouts. Turning off JavaScript or changing the country cannot skip the check.
  • Age rules. Per product, variation and category, and with the product tags 18+ / +18. Tiers 16, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23 and 25. MitID proves 16+ and 18+; higher ages use BankID.
  • Private by design. The plugin never stores the customer’s exact age, CPR number or personnummer.

A VerifyID account is required. Every verification start is billed by VerifyID according to your agreement.

External services

This plugin connects to the VerifyID service, operated by VerifyID ApS (CVR 46325176, Kochsgade 31D, 5000 Odense C, Denmark), and sends the customer to an identity provider. Nothing is sent for carts without age-restricted products unless you turn on the optional age gate: then any visitor who verifies at the gate starts a verification, whatever the cart contains.

VerifyID API (https://app.verifyid.dk/api/)

  • user: when a shop manager saves the key in the setup wizard, clicks “Test connection” or runs wp verifyid test-connection, and after VerifyID refuses a verification start (to tell an unpaid account from an unregistered domain), the plugin sends your plugin key and receives the account status and the account e-mail address. The plugin keeps only the status and a masked copy of the e-mail address. This call is not billed.
  • url_generator_s (MitID) and url_generator_bankid (BankID): when a customer clicks the verify button for a cart that needs age verification, or a visitor verifies at the optional age gate, the plugin sends your plugin key, a random device id, the age being checked (16 to 25) and the return address on your shop’s domain (for MitID also the address to return to after a cancelled login). VerifyID answers with the identity provider’s login address. Each such start is billed.
  • auth_check: when the customer returns, the plugin sends the one-time token and the device id and receives the verification result.

Identity providers. The customer’s browser is redirected to the MitID broker (netseidbroker.dk) or to Nets eID for Swedish BankID (www.ident.nets.eu) and logs in there. The MitID broker (Nets eID Broker) and Nets eID carry out this login for VerifyID as its identity providers and sub-processors; VerifyID’s privacy policy (https://verifyid.dk/privatlivspolitik) describes this processing. The identity provider sends the result to VerifyID, not to your shop. After the login, the identity provider sends the customer’s browser to app.verifyid.dk, which receives the customer’s IP address and browser details and then sends the browser back to your shop.

What VerifyID receives and keeps. VerifyID receives the identity claims returned by MitID or Nets for the person who logs in, including for Swedish BankID the national identity number (personnummer), the person’s age, and your shop’s domain. VerifyID currently keeps a record of every verification (the return address on your shop’s domain, the random device id, the age checked, the result and the times) together with the identity provider’s response, without a fixed deletion date: for MitID the broker’s identifier for the person, for Swedish BankID the full identity response including the personnummer. As the shop owner you are the data controller for your customers: describe this in your privacy policy (the plugin adds suggested text under Settings > Privacy). VerifyID terms of service: https://verifyid.dk/handelsbetingelser. VerifyID privacy policy: https://verifyid.dk/privatlivspolitik. Privacy information for the people who verify: https://verifyid.dk/dpa/slutbruger. Data processing agreement: https://verifyid.dk/dpa.

What the plugin stores in your shop. The method, the proven age tier (for example 18+), the times, a hash of the one-time token and a verification reference on the order; keyed hashes of a browser cookie and of the IP address for abuse limits, which are removed after the retention period you choose. When you let customers declare that their order is delivered outside the countries you verify for, or ask them to tick the age-confirmation checkbox, the plugin also stores that declaration or confirmation with its time and the keyed hash of the browser cookie. The plugin never stores the exact age, the CPR number or the personnummer, and it does not send personal data anywhere else.

Other connections. No CDN is used: the Geist Sans fonts are bundled with the plugin (SIL Open Font License 1.1, see assets/fonts/OFL.txt) and load from your own site, only when the verification pop-up shows. The plugin calls no geolocation service: it only uses WooCommerce’s own geolocation.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install this plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the zip, and activate it.
  3. Open VerifyID > Setup wizard in the WordPress admin menu and follow it: connect your VerifyID key, choose the countries and methods, choose what customers from other countries see, and mark your age-restricted products, categories or tags.
  4. Register every domain your shop uses in the VerifyID dashboard.
sections.faq:
Does the customer have to verify for every order?

No. A verification counts in that browser for the period you choose (60 minutes by default). Logged-in customers can optionally be remembered on their other devices.

Can customers skip the check by turning off JavaScript?

No. The order is checked on the server. Without JavaScript the customer gets a verification page that works with plain forms. While the optional bot challenge applies (Reliability settings: “always”, or “under load” when half of a budget is used), a browser without JavaScript cannot start a verification, because the challenge runs in JavaScript.

What happens if VerifyID is unavailable?

By default, orders with age-restricted products cannot be placed until VerifyID answers again. You can choose to accept them on hold for manual review instead.

I used VerifyID 1.x. Do I lose my settings?

On first start, the plugin reads the 1.x settings it finds: your key, texts, the all-pages setting and product and category ages. wp verifyid migrate --verify checks that every product still has its 1.x age. Category inheritance and tag rules start switched off, because 1.x did not use them; a notice shows how many products would change if you turn them on. After switching, check that the plugin is active on the Plugins screen, then check VerifyID > Settings and the age of a few products. Try the switch on a staging copy of your shop first.

Why do the buttons show the MitID and BankID marks?

The verification pop-up looks like the one of the VerifyID 1.x plugins, including the MitID and BankID marks on its buttons. MitID and BankID are trademarks of their owners. You can replace a mark with a logo you upload under VerifyID > Settings > Appearance.

Which checkouts are covered?

The Checkout block and the classic checkout, the cart, the pay-for-order page and REST API orders, plus adapters for Klarna Checkout (Kustom), Klarna Payments, Nexi Checkout, Svea Checkout, Qliro, Walley, Vipps MobilePay, Stripe, WooCommerce Payments, PayPal Payments and other express buttons. A checkout without an adapter is still protected: an order with age-restricted products that was not verified is put on hold for review. The Compatibility report under VerifyID > Settings > Tools lists what was found on your shop.

Where is the source code of the JavaScript?

The human-readable source of every script in assets/build is included in the plugin, in assets/src. package.json, package-lock.json, webpack.config.js and build/js-build.mjs rebuild assets/build with npm ci && npm run build (Node 22).

Does it work with page caching and cookie banners?

Yes. The verification state is loaded from a request that is never cached, the plugin key never appears in page HTML, and the scripts carry the attributes that the common cookie banners and optimisation plugins use to leave essential scripts alone.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Each site has its own settings, key and data.
sections.changelog:
2.0.1

  • Setup: Live mode can be chosen whatever the VerifyID account status; the status is shown as information.
  • Admin notices show only on the dashboard, Plugins, WooCommerce, VerifyID and Site Health screens.
  • Security hardening: request values are sanitized where they are read, and scripts and styles are printed through the WordPress script and style functions.

2.0.0

  • One plugin for MitID and BankID with location-based method and language, a language switch, server-side enforcement on every order path, the Checkout block, embedded-checkout and express-button support, and an automatic import of 1.x settings.
